city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.p_yest: The high of 35°F was typical for November 13. The normal high for the date is 38°F, and the record is 67°F (1999). The low of 21°F was typical for November 13.
text.t_rec: Duluth has nearly stopped setting record lows
text.p_rec: If Duluth's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Duluth has set 25 standing record lows, far fewer than the 64 that chance alone would give, and 73 record highs, close to the 64 that chance alone would give. The 1930s hold the most record highs of any decade (43). Duluth's all-time high is 106°F, on July 13, 1936.
text.t_chg: Duluth's nights have warmed since 1986. Its days warmed over the long run.
text.p_chg: Across 149 complete years: Duluth's average low shows no clear change: −0.01°F per decade, a range (−0.09 to +0.07) that includes zero. Duluth's average high has risen +0.19°F per decade (95% range +0.13 to +0.26), about +2.9°F since 1875. The last 40 years tell a different story: since 1986, lows have risen +0.82°F per decade (95% range +0.31 to +1.32) and highs show no clear change. The full record joins different observing sites over the years, and a move (for example, from the city to a cooler airport) can hide or exaggerate a long-run trend, so the recent decades are the clearer guide here.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 2 of 12 months; 3 months fell. Highs rose in 7 of 12 months.
text.t_rain: Rain and snow: no clear long-term change
text.p_rain: Duluth's yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (+0.12 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 31.1 inches a year. The wettest year was 1879 (45.38 in); the driest, 1910 (18.11 in).
